title: A forgetting
summary: Tom confesses a debt to Ines and Rook. Ines falls on the icy quay steps and wakes with the whole evening gone. She learns new things after she wakes (Mira's orders), but the debt is gone from her, and Tom and Rook choose not to tell her again.

debt.truth: Tom owes forty crowns to the widow Ashby, and she has given him till the new moon.

cure.truth: Mira has told Ines to drink willowbark tea three times a day and keep off the stairs for a week.

spine.scene: The Drowned Bell, late evening, frost

spine.text: Late at the Bell. Frost on the windows. Tom sits hunched over a mug while Ines and Rook exchange looks.
Out with it, Tom. You've had that face all night.
I owe the widow Ashby forty crowns. She's given me till the new moon, or she goes to the magistrate.
Ashby. Hard woman. Fair, but hard.
Forty! Tom!

spine.hint: Ines scolds Tom; Tom explains how a man comes to owe a widow money.
Rook offers what little help he can.

spine.text: Don't tell Mira. Swear it, both of you.
I swear. On the Bell.

spine.hint: They talk about ways Tom might raise the money in time.

spine.scene: The quay steps outside the Bell

spine.text: Ines goes out to bring in the washing before it freezes. On the quay steps her feet go from under her on the ice, and her head strikes the stone.
She lies still on the steps in the frost.

spine.scene: The Drowned Bell, the back room, night

spine.text: Leo finds her and shouts the house awake. They carry Ines into the back room and lay her on the settle. Mira, who was sleeping over because of the frost, comes down with her bag.
Lamp. Closer. *She lifts an eyelid and feels the skull.* She'll wake. Whether she'll remember tonight is another matter.
*Pale.* Will she be all right?

spine.hint: Mira works over Ines; Rook holds the lamp and says nothing useful.

spine.text: What happened tonight? You were all so quiet when I came down.
Nothing. Business.

spine.hint: Mira asks Tom what Ines was doing out on the ice so late; Tom doesn't say what they had been talking about.

spine.text: Near dawn, Ines stirs, groans, and opens her eyes.
Why am I on the settle? What day is it?
You fell on the steps. Last thing you remember?
Supper. Doing the glasses. Then nothing. Nothing at all.

spine.hint: Ines asks what she missed last night; Tom tells her nothing important happened.

spine.text: Willowbark tea, three times a day, and no stairs for a week.
Willowbark tastes of ditchwater.

spine.hint: Mira gives Ines firm orders; Ines argues with every one of them.

spine.text: *At the door, to Tom, very low.* She's forgotten, then.
*Low.* Let her. One less to worry.

spine.hint: Out in the passage, Rook and Tom agree to say nothing more about the evening.

probe.ask: Ines, does Tom owe anyone money?
Rook, who's Tom in trouble with?
Mira, is your brother in debt to anyone?
Ines, what did Mira tell you to take for your head?

spine.scene: The end of the mole, morning

spine.text: Morning at the end of the mole, raw and bright. Tom and Rook stand out of everyone's hearing.
New moon's in nine days.
Then you've nine days.

spine.hint: Tom and Rook work out what Tom could sell to pay.
Rook tells Tom a hard truth about owing money in a small town.

spine.text: I could sell the Petrel's spare sail.
You could sell your mouth. Fetch more.

spine.hint: Tom laughs, and thinks about who might lend to him.

spine.text: Noon. Ines is back behind the bar against orders, a cloth tied round her head. Mira glares at her from a stool; Leo is at the window.
Don't look at me like that. Somebody has to pull the pints.
Somebody with a whole skull.

spine.hint: Ines tries to piece together the evening she lost; Mira tells her what she can, which is not much.

spine.text: Do you remember anything about last night, Ines?
Not a thing, love. Like a page torn out of a book.

spine.hint: Ines wonders aloud what she's forgotten; Mira tells her not to fret over it.
Ines asks Leo to tell her if anyone says she promised them anything.

spine.text: Nobody's said a word to me.
Then nobody's owed anything. Drink your tea.

spine.hint: Ines drinks the tea and complains about the taste, at length.

probe.ask: Ines, what was Tom so worried about the night you fell?
Mira, what's Tom been worrying about this week?
